title: Three Clinical Factors Predict Prolonged Recovery Duration in Surviving SFTS Patients - Bioengineer.org

analysis.time: The study was published on November 10, 2026. The event date range is from July 2019 to April 2025, during which 43 patients were discharged.
analysis.location_and_population: The study was conducted at Taizhou Hospital of Zhejiang Province, affiliated with Wenzhou Medical University. The population included 43 surviving patients diagnosed with severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS).
analysis.event: A retrospective cohort study identified three clinical factors that independently predicted prolonged recovery duration in surviving SFTS patients. These factors were time from symptom onset to hospital admission, duration of platelet decline, and cardiac or circulatory system involvement. The study was reported by Bioengineer.org.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The mean recovery duration was 16.58 ± 7.86 days, with a median of 15.00 days. The study found that these three factors collectively accounted for 77.62 percent of the variance in recovery time. The disease has case fatality rates between 6 percent and 30 percent, and no licensed vaccine or targeted antiviral medication is available.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study was approved by the Medical Ethics Committee of Taizhou Hospital of Zhejiang Province. The institutional review board waived written informed consent. The research utilized de-identified medical records and standardized inpatient management protocols. The findings are based on a retrospective analysis and are not a direct public health outbreak report.

analysis.brief_en: A retrospective cohort study at Taizhou Hospital of Zhejiang Province, published on November 10, 2026, analyzed recovery durations among 43 surviving patients with severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) who were discharged between July 2019 and April 2025. The study identified three clinical factors that independently predicted prolonged recovery: time from symptom onset to hospital admission, duration of platelet decline, and cardiac or circulatory system involvement. These factors collectively accounted for 77.62% of the variance in recovery time, as determined by a backward stepwise multiple linear regression model. The mean recovery duration was 16.58 ± 7.86 days, with a median of 15 days. SFTS is an acute bunyavirus infection with case fatality rates ranging from 6% to 30% across regions. The study highlights the importance of these factors in understanding hospital resource use and rehabilitation needs, as no licensed vaccine or targeted antiviral medication exists for SFTS. The research was approved by the hospital's ethics committee and used de-identified medical records without direct patient contact.

title: Climate Shifts Projected to Expand SFTS Tick Habitats in Eastern China - Bioengineer.org

analysis.time: The study was conducted between 2019 and 2024, with future projections extending to 2040 and 2060. The article was published on November 9, 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The research focused on Jiangsu Province, eastern China, examining tick habitats and their relationship to SFTS. The study included rural villages, country parks, urban parks, and forest parks.
analysis.event: A long-term surveillance and ecological modeling study projected that climate shifts will expand the habitats suitable for ticks transmitting SFTS in eastern China. The study analyzed tick distribution and climate-driven changes in habitat suitability.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The study found that Haemaphysalis longicornis accounted for 89.1% of collected ticks, and Haemaphysalis flava for 9.8%. Future projections indicated a 336.5% increase in high-suitability areas for Haemaphysalis longicornis between 2021 and 2040, and a 640.3% increase between 2041 and 2060. For Haemaphysalis flava, the increase was 91.4% and 118.8% respectively. These changes suggest a significant expansion of tick habitats, potentially increasing the risk of SFTS transmission.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study used an optimized MaxEnt modeling framework and field monitoring to analyze tick distribution and climate-driven habitat shifts. The findings highlight the need for integrating climate-sensitive vector surveillance into SFTS prevention strategies. The research is based on surveillance records and projections, indicating ongoing investigation and analysis.

analysis.brief_en: A study published on November 9, 2026, by Bioengineer.org highlights the potential expansion of tick habitats transmitting Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome (SFTS) in eastern China due to climate shifts. Conducted between 2019 and 2024 in Jiangsu Province, the research analyzed tick distribution and climate-driven changes in habitat suitability. The study found that Haemaphysalis longicornis accounted for 89.1% of collected ticks, while Haemaphysalis flava made up 9.8%. Future projections under the SSP245 scenario suggest a 336.5% increase in high-suitability areas for Haemaphysalis longicornis between 2021 and 2040, and a 640.3% increase between 2041 and 2060. For Haemaphysalis flava, the increases were 91.4% and 118.8% respectively. These findings indicate a significant shift in tick habitats, which could increase the risk of SFTS transmission. The study emphasizes the importance of integrating climate-sensitive vector surveillance into SFTS prevention strategies within a One Health framework.

title: A virus found in one out of ten patients in China is carried by a tick species that is spreading across the US

analysis.time: The study was reported in September 2026 (N8), and the tick species spread in the U.S. by October 2025 (N38). The publication date is 2026-11-07 (N1).
analysis.location_and_population: The research was conducted in China, testing patients and ticks from 15 provinces (N2, N26). The tick species, Asian longhorned tick, has spread to parts of the United States (N31, N38, N40).
analysis.event: A newly identified tick-borne virus, ALTNV, was found in 10.4 percent of 3,163 patients tested in China (N1). It was also detected in ticks collected from 15 provinces (N2).
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Among 38 patients infected with both ALTNV and DBV, 18.4 percent died (N23). Patients with ALTNV alone had mild symptoms and fully recovered (N19).
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study was published in the New England Journal of Medicine (N51). The CDC noted that the full public health and agricultural impact of the tick's spread is unknown (N37).

analysis.brief_en: A study published in September 2026 in the New England Journal of Medicine revealed that a newly identified tick-borne virus, Asian longhorned tick nairovirus (ALTNV), was found in 10.4 percent of 3,163 patients tested in China. ALTNV was also detected in ticks from 15 provinces. The virus belongs to the genus Orthonairovirus and shares less than 80 percent amino acid similarity with other species in the same genus (N13, N14). Among 38 patients coinfected with ALTNV and Dabie bandavirus (DBV), 18.4 percent died, while those infected with ALTNV alone had mild symptoms and fully recovered (N23, N19). The Asian longhorned tick, which carries ALTNV, has spread to parts of the United States, with the U.S. Department of Agriculture documenting its presence in 21 states by October 2025 (N38, N40). The CDC emphasized that the full public health and agricultural impact of this tick's spread remains unknown (N37).
